author: Declaration Desk
title: Gadkari promises 250-km Kolkata ring road, opens Rs 8,700 crore of Bengal highway work
dek: At Kolaghat, the Union road minister launched 22 national highway projects and announced a Rs 14,000 crore ring road around Kolkata. Reports give different totals for his wider package, and no sanction order has been published.
body:
Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari on Thursday inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 22 national highway projects worth about Rs 8,700 crore in West Bengal, and announced a 250-km ring road around Kolkata at an estimated cost of Rs 14,000 crore. Speaking at Kolaghat in Purba Medinipur alongside Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, he said Bengal's roads would be transformed within five years.

The ring road is the headline promise for Kolkata, whose traffic has grown far faster than its road space. According to reports, it would link Howrah with North and South 24 Parganas and join up the Kona, Belghoria and Kalyani expressways. Mr Gadkari also set out a much larger pipeline of expressways and corridors for the state, which reports variously totalled at Rs 75,000 crore and Rs 1 lakh crore. No detailed project report, sanction order or timetable for the ring road has been made public, and the ministry had not published a release on the event by Friday morning.

## What happened

The 22 projects launched on Thursday, a mix of completed stretches opened and new works begun, include the six-laning of the Palsit-Dankuni section of NH-19, the main highway between Kolkata and Delhi, and a new four-lane bridge over the Ganga downstream of the Farakka Barrage, according to reports. The rest are spread across Purba Medinipur, Birbhum, Purba Bardhaman, Purulia, Hooghly, North and South 24 Parganas and Paschim Bardhaman, with four projects to strengthen existing national highways. In a post on X, Mr Gadkari described the event as the inauguration and ground-breaking of the 22 projects; he did not itemise their lengths or completion dates.

He then went further. According to one detailed account of his speech, he listed:

- Kolkata ring road: 250 km, about Rs 14,000 crore
- Dankuni-Kolaghat eight-lane highway: about Rs 20,000 crore
- Varanasi-Kolkata greenfield expressway: Rs 30,000 crore for the 235-km Bengal section, through Purulia, Bankura, Paschim Medinipur, Hooghly and Howrah, with its project report sent to the Union Cabinet
- Gorakhpur-Siliguri expressway: about Rs 38,000 crore
- Siliguri-Guwahati high-speed corridor: about Rs 26,000 crore
- Raxaul-Haldia expressway, Bengal portion: about Rs 17,000 crore
- Moregram-Kishanganj corridor: about Rs 12,000 crore

He also asked the state to prepare a project report for multi-tier flyovers carrying a metro line on a single row of pillars, of the kind built in Nagpur and Pune, and said Bengal would be helped with about 10,000 electric vehicles, according to reports.

"I want to make Kolkata a better city," he said, adding that after Mumbai and Delhi, it was now Kolkata's turn. He said he had come to tell the chief minister "not to worry" about money, and that he would visit every six months to check progress, reports said.

## The numbers do not yet add up

The announcements mix projects at very different stages. The Rs 8,700 crore for the 22 projects is the only figure that every account agrees on. Mr Adhikari said Bengal was set to receive Centre-funded road projects worth Rs 25,000 crore, according to reports, while on 11 November he had said Mr Gadkari would lay foundation stones for projects worth Rs 20,000 crore during this visit. Reports of the wider package differ between Rs 75,000 crore and Rs 1 lakh crore, and several of the corridors listed, including the Gorakhpur-Siliguri and Raxaul-Haldia expressways, run mostly outside Bengal. Readers should treat the larger totals as announced intentions rather than money sanctioned.

## Background

Kolkata has talked about a ring road for years. In March 2023 the previous state government proposed an outer ring road of about 200 km in the Kolkata-Howrah region at a cost of around Rs 4,000 crore, running from Barajaguli on NH-34 to Bishnupur on NH-117 via Dankuni, Uluberia and Budge Budge, with a large share of the money for a bridge at Budge Budge, according to an industry report at the time. That plan did not get off the ground.

The Varanasi-Kolkata expressway shows how such projects stall. The Centre cleared its original alignment with the state's consent in January 2023, but the state later asked for a change, and a revised alignment was approved only in October 2024. Mr Gadkari told the Rajya Sabha last year that construction could not begin in Bengal because the state government had revised the alignment, while work moved ahead in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand, according to reports.

Land has been the other obstacle. In earlier years Mr Gadkari had sought the then chief minister's help to speed up land acquisition for national highway projects in Bengal. On Thursday Mr Adhikari said land arrangements for the projects launched were complete, according to reports.

## What they are saying

The event was framed politically. Mr Gadkari said the "double-engine" train, the BJP's phrase for the same party governing the state and the Centre, would "transform Bengal", according to reports. Mr Adhikari said Bengal lagged behind other states in national highway coverage and had been denied its due share over the past 15 years because of poor coordination between the previous state government and the Centre, according to reports. He said all district headquarters would be linked by four-lane roads, and asked for a road link from Kakdwip towards Gangasagar for the annual mela, which Mr Gadkari said would be approved.

No response from opposition parties to the announcements had been reported by Friday morning.

## What it means for Kolkata and the districts

If built, a ring road would let freight heading between the ports at Kolkata and Haldia, the Delhi highway and north Bengal skirt the city instead of crossing it, which is the main purpose of such roads in other metros. The Dankuni-Kolaghat widening and the Palsit-Dankuni six-laning address the most crowded approaches to Kolkata from the west. The Farakka bridge and the Siliguri-Guwahati corridor matter for north Bengal, whose links to the rest of India run through the narrow Siliguri Corridor.

## What happens next

- The state has been asked to prepare project reports for the flyover-metro corridors; the ring road's report, alignment and cost estimate are yet to be published.
- The Varanasi-Kolkata expressway's Bengal section awaits the Union Cabinet's decision on its project report.
- Mr Gadkari said he would return in six months to review progress.
